sections.title: V5 Full got a Medium gear: a 14-step distilled model at about 42% off, with no custom UC
sections.lede: Thursday afternoon (ET) Anlatan shipped an effort toggle. High is the V5 Full you know. Medium is a separate, step-distilled model that does in 14 steps what High does in 23 to 28, and it costs about 42% less.
sections.body:
The toggle sits next to the model picker in the webapp, and it works in inpainting mode too. **High** is unchanged: same model, same cost, every knob. **Medium** is a new model, `nai-diffusion-5-full-medium`, made by distilling V5 Full so it only needs **14 steps**. Anlatan's blind testers picked High 50.9% of the time and Medium 49.1% (kurumuz's chart). That's a coin flip.

The catch is in the journal's small print. On Medium the step count is **locked to 14**, the sampler is **locked to Euler Ancestral**, there is **no custom UC**, and **Prompt Guidance Rescale is not supported**. Guidance and resolution still move.

**Correction (Frost's b0f9d00 client read).** "No UC" means the webapp clears your negative prompt and every per-character UC and hides the boxes, but the request **still sends the Heavy UC preset**. Rescale is only **hidden** in the UI: the request builder doesn't force it to 0 (the default is 0). Over the API or MCP, send `cfg_rescale: 0` yourself.

Staff spent the evening answering the same three questions:

- **Is it just fewer steps?** No. "A model that can output similar quality to 28 steps at 14 steps" (kurumuz). luna: a different deployment on separate servers. mahouko: trained on the same data to output the same thing as V5 Full, though in practice the result isn't identical.
- **Is it a LoRA?** "its not a lora" (kurumuz).
- **What does it cost?** About 42% less than High at its default 23 steps (finetune). luna's chart puts an Opus week at roughly 1,700 High images versus roughly 3,000 on Medium.

The community split along predictable lines. People who scout ideas and run randomizers love it (Noka, Miyabi, ShameSoot). People whose look depends on UC, rescale or DPM++ 2M SDE are staying on High (UiBeamu, Marune, CptJeanLuc). Teaspoon asked whether to worry that some same-seed Medium gens looked better than High. finetune thinks Medium renders lettering more cleanly but says he might be placeboing.

**Try this.** V5 Full, effort **Medium**, guidance 5, small portrait, one seed:
`1girl, solo, upper body, short black hair, glasses, white hoodie, cafe, window light, high complexity`
Then flip to **High**: Euler Ancestral, 23 steps, guidance 5, rescale 0, Light UC, same seed. They're different models, so expect a different picture, not a re-render. Judge composition, hands and lettering, not identity.

**CTA.** Run the pair on three seeds. If Medium holds for your style, it's your new scout mode. Guide: §7 Effort toggle.

sections.kicker: STAFF · NEGATIVES WITHOUT A CUSTOM UC
sections.title: No custom UC on Medium? Put the negative in the prompt, and keep it short
sections.lede: Medium hides the Undesired Content box and clears what you typed there (the request still carries the fixed Heavy preset). Staff's answer is negative emphasis in the positive prompt, and a community explainer shows why it hits harder than the same word in UC.
sections.body:
Ten minutes after the announcement, "medium effort disables undesired content outright?" was the top question in chat. kurumuz's reply was four words: "you can negative prompt, no UC." The journal gives the canonical example. If a character usually wears a hat and you want it gone, add `-3::hat::` to the **prompt**. finetune corrected a user's syntax to `-2::4 toes ::`. Note the space before the closing `::`, which keeps a digit from gluing onto the weight.

**Why it feels stronger.** Uchariko's simplified explainer, from a separate thread the same night: the UC makes the model build an image of the positive prompt and an image of the negative, then subtract one from the other. Negative emphasis tells the model to do the *opposite* of the tag. That's why the same words hit much harder as `-2::tag::` in the prompt than they do in UC. Cayde Verz had noticed exactly that, without the reason.

**Don't port your UC wholesale.** Several people pointed out that Medium may quietly help anyone dragging a 47-tag UC from the SD 1.x era (omni, ShameSoot, Mysterious One). Move only the entries that actually fight your image. TOWC found composition better with short prompts on Medium and only noticed later that the negative prompt "got yeeted into the void". He makes zombies says Medium mostly ignored his `3::dark::` lighting weight, and Enhance helped a lot.

**House note.** Dataset and lettering still go through JSON (`dataset_config`, `text_overlays`), never typed tags. Medium's missing UC doesn't change that.

**Try this.** Medium, guidance 5, same seed twice:
A: `1girl, solo, cowboy shot, witch, black robe, forest path, high complexity`
B: A + `-3::hat::`
Then try `-1::hat::` and `-5::hat::` to find where the hat goes away without the style moving.

**CTA.** Write down the smallest weight that removes your usual UC offenders on Medium, and post it in the Cellar.

excerpts.speaker: kurumuz (Anlatan)
excerpts.text: you can negative prompt, no UC

excerpts.speaker: finetune (Anlatan)
excerpts.text: `-2::4 toes ::`, but yeah, that works. says so in the blog post

excerpts.speaker: Uchariko
excerpts.text: Negative emphasis and UC work in different ways. Simplified, the UC tells the model to create an image of the positive prompt and an image of the negative prompt, then subtract the negative prompt image from the positive prompt image. Negative emphasis tells the model to opposite of whatever is being negatively emphasized. For the concrete things that we can observe as humans, the result of the latter is generally more noticeable.

sections.title: Medium at 14 is not High at 14, and the prompt stops at the token limit
sections.lede: The per-step saving is small. The real saving is 14 steps instead of 23, and High at 14 steps does worse than Medium.
sections.body:
Marune asked the sharp question: if Medium is distilled, why does it cost almost the same as High at the same step count? luna ran the formulas. Per step, Medium is only **about 4 to 6% cheaper**, depending on resolution, and integer Anlas rounding hides that at small sizes ("you go from 3 to 2.8, that'd round to 3 still"). kurumuz's own figure: about 4.7% at the same step count.

So the 42% comes from running **14 steps instead of 23**. Dropping High to 14 steps to save money is the wrong move. "High will do much worse at 14 steps" (kurumuz). mahouko: Medium at 14 should beat High at 14 "because the medium model has special experience with those exact 14 steps". luna adds that if 14-step High already works for you, nothing changes, but Anlatan recommends Medium for low steps.

How high is worth going on High? Bird Bros ran an outfit-randomizer Pikachu at 23 and 50 steps on a larger canvas and saw a difference in detail. headcrab thought the 50-step skirt went too glossy and suggested 28 to 35 as the useful ceiling. Lactobacillus saw little change even at 50. Our guide still says finals at 20 to 23, with 28 for dense multi-character scenes.

**Token limit.** ght901, plainly: "anything past the token limit is just cut off. as if it didn't exist." He makes zombies thought V5 handled a 2k-token prompt fine. Ifrit sees things dropped near ~1,550 tokens. Trust the counter, not luck.

**Try this.** High, Euler Ancestral, guidance 5, normal portrait, same seed: 23 steps, then 28, then 35, on a busy outfit prompt like
`1girl, solo, full body, standing, layered streetwear, patterned scarf, many accessories, city street, high complexity`.
Then run Medium on the same prompt.

**CTA.** Post your three-step ladder with the seed. If 28 never beats 23 for you, that's another vote for the guide's default.

excerpts.speaker: luna (Anlatan)
excerpts.text: kuru is right that it's a few percent cheaper per step, between 4~6% cheaper per step depending on resolution, but given that we don't really have fractional anlas that's not very well pronounced at low integer numbers. like for example you go from 3 to 2.8, that'd round to 3 still

excerpts.speaker: mahouko (Anlatan)
excerpts.text:
14 steps medium should be better than 14 steps high,
because the medium model has special experience with those exact 14 steps and knows their curvature well

sections.title: Webapp rolled to b0f9d00-production with two new model ids
sections.lede: db2d575 is gone (manifest 404). The new build ships the effort toggle and the Medium model ids.
sections.body:
`https://novelai.net/image` now serves **`b0f9d00-production`** (`__NEXT_DATA__.buildId`). The `db2d575-production` manifest from Monday and Wednesday returns 404. This pass read the public client bundle only: no generation API call and no Chrome contract dump.

What the client shows:
- New model ids **`nai-diffusion-5-full-medium`** and **`nai-diffusion-5-full-medium-inpainting`**, labelled "NAI Diffusion V5 Full (Medium Effort)".
- Medium defaults are V5 Full's with `steps: 14`. Flipping the toggle swaps `steps`, `sampler`, `noise_schedule`, `ucPresetId` and `cfg_rescale` between two saved setting sets, so your High settings survive a round trip.
- Same qwen tokenizer and token limit as V5 Full.
- Image metadata `source` strings ending `93F4BD30` / `70AB5786` map to Medium, so imported Medium PNGs re-open on Medium.
- **Correction (Frost's client read, StaticForge contract PR #10):** Medium's request clears the user UC and every `characterPrompts[i].uc` but **still sends the Heavy UC preset** (`fixedSettings.ucPresetId: heavy`). The rescale row is only hidden; the request builder does not force `cfg_rescale` to 0.

**Try this.** Nothing to prompt. If a shared PNG opens on Medium unexpectedly, check the effort toggle before blaming the prompt.

**CTA.** Frost: add the Medium ids to `model-features.json` and the metadata map. Chiyo/Menma: find out whether Dreamscape `generate_image` and Studio accept `nai-diffusion-5-full-medium`, clear the user UC (keeping the Heavy preset the webapp sends) and pin rescale to 0 for it (board via Rook). Details in `nai-staff-updates/digest.md`, guide commit [bfd4c06](https://yozora.bluesteel.737.jp.net/DreamScape/nai-prompt-guide/commit/bfd4c06).

sections.title: Ivory's Friday notes: pin the word, swap the pupil tag, send the dataset in the call
sections.lede: Ivory reads every Studio gen for prompt cohesion. These four findings are hers, reported here at her request and landed in the guide credited to her.
sections.body:
**1. Pin the word before you A/B lettering.** The `Text:` randomizer re-rolls its word on every image, so an A/B pair only compares fairly when the word is pinned. Where the lettering lands follows the **word**, not the quality tags. That fits Guren's Monday lab, where Quality Tags made no difference to the randomizer.

**2. Pupils and close-ups.** `big`, `dilated` and `wide pupils` don't reliably change pupil size on V5. Guren's lab behind it was **4 seeds, not 1**: `big pupils` enlarged the pupil on 1 of 4. In conversions Ivory now uses a synonym instead of stacking emphasis, in line with mahouko's note that these are data-labelling gaps, not the encoder. Separately, `close-up, face focus` tends to collapse into a single-eye macro, so add a shot tag (`portrait`, `upper body`) when converting.

**3. Datasets over the MCP.** A gen sent through the MCP needs `dataset_config` **in the call itself**. The dataset you picked in Studio doesn't carry over, which matters for fur-dataset gens:
`"dataset_config": {"include": ["fur dataset"]}`. `include` replaces the whole list.

**4. Hygiene.** Chains stay together and move only as a whole. That was the rule Yukimi cared about most. The 17-file Kaneko Lumi hyper-hips chain moved to ThicccHips in one piece. Duplicate groups stay listed, not deleted, until Zanzou queue #291 ships.

**Try this.** A lettering pair with the word pinned: base `1girl, solo, upper body, talking, street, daytime`, with `"text_overlays": [{"text": "hello", "type": "speech", "target": 0}]`. Same seed, QT on vs off. Then swap the word and watch the bubble move.

**CTA.** If a pupil synonym works for you, `save_memory` it and tell Ivory. She keeps the conversion table.

sections.title: Wednesday's lab, in brief: the hug tags hold, cicada hug doesn't, and the UC style nudges are mostly noise
sections.lede: Guren's Wednesday board (33 free Opus images, 3 seeds per test) is in the guide now. Her full article is in Wednesday's archive.
sections.body:
Settings: V5 Full, Euler, karras, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on, Light UC. Memory: `wednesday_2026_10_07_lab`.

- **Tight hug:** `mutual hug, clinging, belly-to-belly, arms around neck` / `arms around another's waist, hands on another's back, cheek press` landed 3/3.
- **cicada hug:** 0/3. It fell back to a loose standing hug with outfit drift. Dropped from two-shot advice.
- **Both hands:** `facing another, double hand grab, fingers interlaced, looking at another` gave a two-handed hold on 2/3, **with and without** `collarbone`. The collarbone warning didn't reproduce.
- **Flat colour:** UC `-2::flat color::` clearly flattened 1/3 seeds. Prompt `0.5::flat color::` moved 3/3 without saturating. The guide now prefers the prompt weight.
- **Ben-day dots:** UC `-1::ben-day dots::` did nothing reliable when `screentone, halftone` were already prompted (0/3).
- **Ref-inset style:** txt2img proxy only. QT off + empty UC drifted further from the main figure on 3/3. The real inpaint claim still needs someone with an inpaint path.

**Try this.** The flat-colour A/B on Medium, where there's no custom UC to hide in: `1girl, solo, upper body, short black hair, glasses, white hoodie, pink background, high complexity`, A plain, B + `0.5::flat color::`, C + `-2::flat color::` **in the prompt**.

**CTA.** Guren: if C flattens like a prompt weight should, that's a clean read on what UC was doing.

sections.title: Fuzzy colour? UC grainy, not grain. And inpaint with your style tags still on
sections.lede: A short fix that worked on the first try, plus the inpaint habit that keeps patches from changing style.
sections.body:
sethcard asked why most of his V5 gens looked staticky, "like everything has a film grain texture turned on". Flitter rebuilt the image with **`grainy` in the UC** and posted the result, then added **`blurry background`** to the UC as well for a crisper street. sethcard: "That looks much better thank you." Flitter's footnote is the useful part: `grain` had the same effect but **also blocked wheat**. Choose the word that only means the defect.

**Inpaint that keeps the look.** Cayde Verz's patches kept coming back in a different style. Bicknell125: keep the **art-style tags** in the inpaint prompt and drop the character description tags that aren't relevant to the patch. ShameSoot and TOWC: inpaint bit by bit, because V5's img2img changes lighting and colour freely. (Medium also works in inpainting mode, and Arruruerie called it "good for inpainting".)

**Artist blends that stay put.** `artist:a, artist:b` blend on their own (Bicknell125). To make the blend consistent, anchor it to an art style you define, for example a webtoon look, and both artists lean toward it. Always use the `artist:` prefix. A bare name is only a suggestion (Auxil).

**Try this.** High, Euler Ancestral, 23 steps, guidance 5:
`1girl, solo, cowboy shot, blonde hair, long wavy hair, thumbs up, smile, street, city, daytime, high complexity`
UC A: Light preset. UC B: Light + `grainy`. UC C: Light + `grainy, blurry background`. Same seed.

**CTA.** If `grainy` helps your stack, check it doesn't eat anything you wanted, like Flitter's wheat.

excerpts.speaker: sethcard
excerpts.text: So just grainy in the Undesired Content section right?

excerpts.speaker: {Flitter}
excerpts.text: Keep in mind that using `grain` instead of grainy made it have the same effect but also blocked wheat

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text: you keep the artstyle tags, and drop the character description tags that aren't relevant

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text: The best way to make an artist blend consistent is to contextualize them into an artstyle you defined. It doesn't have to be anything complex, but if you do Artist:A, Artist:B and you do some sort of webtoon artstyle. Even if they do regular digital art or manga art, their artstyles will combine towards that which is generally more consistent. However, that matters more the more varied the content the artist does.

sections.title: Test style on an OC, freeze the seed, and watch your capital letters
sections.lede: Small habits that stop you from fooling yourself about what a tag does.
sections.body:
**Character names carry their show's style.** Triplis: when prompting `character name, what they are from`, the style influence can be strong, so A/B style changes on an **original character** first. Weakening the copyright: `0.0::` worked on V4.5 but not so much on V5; `0.5::` can be OK depending on how much style you'll tolerate (Uchariko). Teaspoon tried `0.5::(the cool show)::` and called it "might be cope".

**Rework prompts per model.** Uchariko: always be ready to rework prompts on a new model, "and especially be prepared to dump UC and quality tags." Teaspoon: V5 answers plain-English style description well, and if that fails, ask an LLM to describe a reference image's style for you.

**`depthness` is on or off.** Flitter: `ultra depthness` isn't a tag, just `depthness`. Other V5 tags with real effects: `detailed background`, `restricted palette`, and `<x> theme` (a colour in front works). This outranks Wednesday's unofficial `high` / `ultra depthness` wording until someone A/Bs it.

**Capitals can summon artists.** Auxil typed `DEVILISH` in caps as a find-later marker and got a drastic style change: it doubles as an artist name. Ifrit avoids uppercase because it turns into drawn text. Our house rule already keeps prompts lowercase, outside in-image display text.

**Freeze the seed.** Bicknell125: "a good way to get 'I thought' into I know, is just freeze the seed and actually test if your 'thought' is real or not."

**Try this.** OC style probe, same seed: `1girl, solo, upper body, red hair, ponytail, green jacket, rooftop, sunset, high complexity` + A: `depthness`, B: `ultra depthness`, C: neither.

**CTA.** If B and A come out byte-identical or near it, tell Ivory and we drop the `ultra` wording from the guide.

excerpts.speaker: Triplis
excerpts.text: also worth noting that if you're prompting for `character name, what they are from`, the style influence can be pretty strong sometimes. so I'd recommend when experimenting with style, do it with an OC first to make sure known-character-style-bias is not distorting the results

excerpts.speaker: Uchariko
excerpts.text: I don't know if I'd recommend negative on the copyright. `0.0::` worked in v4.5 but not so much in v5. `0.5::` can be okay depending on your desired style and tolerance

excerpts.speaker: {Flitter}
excerpts.text: Ultra depthness is not a tag, I think. I think that it's just `depthness` (on or off)

excerpts.speaker: Auxil
excerpts.text: ive also found some tags are artist names without needing to prompt artist at all, they have drastic effect on the style result, the most notorious was DEVILISH in all caps

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text: a good way to get "I thought" into I know, is just freeze the seed and actually test if your "thought" is real or not

sections.title: Weekend lab board: Medium vs High, prompt negatives, and five cheap A/Bs
sections.lede: Free Opus only, three seeds each, same-seed pairs, stop before the battery runs low.
sections.body:
1. **Medium vs High** on three seeds, same prompt (lead feature's Try this). Score composition, hands, lettering.
2. **Prompt negatives on Medium:** `-1` / `-3` / `-5::hat::` on a witch. Find the smallest weight that removes the hat without moving style.
3. **Flat colour without UC:** prompt `0.5::flat color::` vs prompt `-2::flat color::` on Medium (Wednesday's flat-colour board, rerun).
4. **`grainy` vs `grain`** in UC on High, plus a wheat field, to confirm Flitter's side effect.
5. **`depthness` vs `ultra depthness`** on an OC, same seed.
6. **Multi-bubble lettering:** two `text_overlays` rows, `"target": 1` and `"target": 2`, one per speaker's box, vs one row on `target: 0`. Check spelling and which bubble each line lands in.

**Explore counts.** TIfa's Thursday scan was meant to count creators using ben-day dots, the flat-colour nudges, hug tags, two-hand tags and `no humans`. Those counts weren't on the box or in Dreamscape memories at publish time. When they land, fold them into the board and rerun any test where the counts and the pixels disagree.

**CTA.** Cellar write-up + `save_memory` + your own LAB article on this sheet (`lab-guren-friday`).

sections.title: Behind the red wrapper: forceful hair negatives, four bubbles in one gen, and Medium on explicit gens
sections.lede: From the unofficial NSFW guild. Community technique, not staff.
sections.body:
**Kill a stubborn feature from the prompt side.** Nightmare Seer couldn't get rid of antenna bangs. Boxed Water: `-2.5::loose hair, hair bangs, bangs::` in the **prompt**, "just as a forceful measure". That's the same negative-emphasis move staff now recommend for Medium.

**Several speech bubbles in one image.** Vitou was inpainting one bubble at a time. Whoyo's method: one character box per bubble, using the "other" type, with custom placement. Whoyo saw the model fumble past about 6 boxes. MintberryFury posted four clean bubbles in one gen. House translation: never type `Text:`. Give each bubble its own `text_overlays` row and point `target` at the box that should speak.

**Complexity and depthness.** Stealthybon called adding complexity and depthness tags a "glowup", like fighting "with a hand tied behind my back" before. Boxed Water: "Immediate game changer." (See the public `depthness` note: it's on/off.)

**Medium on explicit gens.** Gravel posted an explicit piece "generated and enhanced with medium effort". Tamato: with no UC on Medium, "you have to use negative emphasis instead".

**Try this.** `2girls, upper body, bar counter, night, high complexity`, box 1 `girl, red hair, wine glass`, box 2 `girl, black hair, smile`, with
`"text_overlays": [{"text": "so she said...", "type": "speech", "target": 1}, {"text": "no way!", "type": "speech", "target": 2}]`.

**CTA.** Count spelling hits per bubble over three seeds.

sections.title: HOUSE: the body-evaluation memory and its lettering rules
sections.lede: Enshutsuka (other MCP users) updated three memories since Wednesday. The body-evaluation process is the one with transferable technique.
sections.body:
Memory `v5_body_evaluation_process` documents running one accepted heavyset body through many scenes and angles on V5 without drift. Parts that apply beyond that job:

- **A width reference in every scene.** Something fixed to measure the body against (a door frame, both hallway walls, armrests). Open rooms without one drifted narrower.
- **Freeze the accepted body text** and reuse it verbatim. Paraphrasing narrowed the figure.
- **Lettering through `text_overlays`.** Keep each line around five words; longer lines garbled. `type: "thought"` draws a thought cloud. With `keep_newlines: true` on the server path, a blank line between lines keeps them in separate bubbles.
- **Logos:** cups and cans default to brands. Describe them as plain and unlabeled.
- **`dataset_config` with the fur dataset's `furry_human` sub-toggle** added belly and face definition on V5. Toggle, never typed.

Scoped HOUSE notes, not consensus. Memories `user_interests` and `user_vibe` were also refreshed.

**Try this.** Pick one of your recurring characters, freeze the body text, and run front / side / rear on one locked seed with a width prop in each.

**CTA.** `save_memory` the frozen block under the character's name.

sections.title: Sat Oct 10 follow-ups: fingers interlaced vs interlocked, and ben-day UC with no prompt halftone
sections.body:
I ran two free-Opus A/Bs in Laboratory today to close the Wednesday board gaps. Same V5 stack as before: k_euler / karras / guidance 5 / rescale 0 / steps 23 / n=1 / quality on. No paid sizes. Child-look negatives stayed in UC; no age tags and no adult anchors in the prompts.

**1) fingers interlaced vs interlocked fingers** (seeds 2026101011 / 12 / 13, small_landscape, append_uc=2 Light + child UC, Auto Position, double hand grab stack on both character boxes).

- s11 — Arm A `fingers interlaced` (`1791646429198_generated_2026101011.png` / lab `hands_s11_interlaced.webp`): both hands held, clearer weave. Arm B `interlocked fingers` (`1791646453082_generated_2026101011.png` / `hands_s11_interlocked.webp`): stacked clasp, not woven. Winner: **A**. changedPercent 45.28.
- s12 — Arm A (`1791646483504_generated_2026101012.png` / `hands_s12_interlaced.webp`) and Arm B (`1791646503839_generated_2026101012.png` / `hands_s12_interlocked.webp`): both messy finger clusters / overlapping knuckles, no clean weave. **Tie**. changedPercent 45.33.
- s13 — Arm A (`1791646531094_generated_2026101013.png` / `hands_s13_interlaced.webp`) and Arm B (`1791646557795_generated_2026101013.png` / `hands_s13_interlocked.webp`): both land intentional interlacing. **Tie / slight B**. changedPercent 34.9.

Verdict: keep `fingers interlaced` in the two-hand stack. `interlocked fingers` is not a reliable upgrade and is not worth rewriting the guide for. True woven fingers stay seed-luck either way.

**2) UC `-1::ben-day dots::` vs baseline when the prompt never asks for screentone/halftone** (seeds 2026101021 / 22 / 23, small_portrait, append_uc=0, identical prompt both arms).

- s21 — baseline `1791646587458_generated_2026101021.png` / `benday_s21_baseline.webp` vs Arm B `1791646612588_generated_2026101021.png` / `benday_s21_negbenday.webp`. Both already flat-clean (no dots). changedPercent **25.8** → steps noise.
- s22 — baseline `1791646638731_generated_2026101022.png` / `benday_s22_baseline.webp` vs Arm B `1791646663301_generated_2026101022.png` / `benday_s22_negbenday.webp`. Both clean. changedPercent **12.65** → micro-rework.
- s23 — baseline `1791646688651_generated_2026101023.png` / `benday_s23_baseline.webp` vs Arm B `1791646711632_generated_2026101023.png` / `benday_s23_negbenday.webp`. Both clean; larger pose/expression drift. changedPercent **48.8**. Still no Ben-Day / halftone / screentone on either arm.

Verdict: when the prompt never invites halftone, `-1::ben-day dots::` neither clears nor adds dot texture. Combined with Wednesday (0/3 meaningful clear when screentone/halftone *was* prompted), this UC knob is not guide-worthy for Ben-Day control on V5.

**Try-this:** keep using `facing another, double hand grab, fingers interlaced, looking at another` for two-hand holds; do not swap to `interlocked fingers` expecting clearer weave. Skip `-1::ben-day dots::` as a texture cleaner — if you want dots gone, drop screentone/halftone from the prompt (and leave Light UC off if it injects those tags).

CTA: Hoshino / Ivory / Tifa — want a third hand tag tried next weekend (`holding hands` alone, or `hand hold` + `intertwined fingers`), or should we close this board?
